control_mechanism: separately-declared C translation units disagree on a shared struct's field layout, silently corrupting cross-TU by-value data even though the linker succeeds -- linker success is not ABI evidence
a partial-initialization/cleanup path releases fewer resources than it acquired when an intermediate acquisition stage fails, or on the success path
a cleanup path releases the same set of acquired resources it should, but not in the required reverse-of-acquisition order
a release is routed through an allocator identity different from the one that performed the matching allocation, and the mismatch is accepted instead of rejected
a foreign boundary retains a raw pointer to a borrowed buffer past its owner's release and dereferences it after the owner generation has ended
a false `restrict`/no-alias promise on a parameter that is actually aliased diverges between -O0 and -O3 under optimization

a concrete heap use-after-free is silent undefined behavior under a plain -O0/-O3 execution -- not a guaranteed crash, since the freed block is often re-served intact -- and requires a sanitizer's deterministic redzone/quarantine trap to become observable at all

`-fno-sanitize-recover=all` silently fails to take effect (for example a typo'd options string), letting UBSan continue past a real violation instead of aborting with a report -- a clean sanitizer run is not evidence unless this itself is proven

a foreign nonlocal exit (a `longjmp` past an acquiring frame) bypasses ordinary lexical cleanup and produces NO sanitizer report at all -- zero ASan/UBSan diagnostics -- which is the load-bearing caution distinguishing this hazard from every other Phase 5 sanitizer-detected defect: the sanitizer lane cannot see it by construction, so its live descendant is Phase 4's own nonlocal-exit control, not the Phase 5 sanitizer lane
